Seminar Title:

Isolation, Modification, and Characterization of Guar Germ Proteins for Emulsion-based Application

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Food Process Engineering

Speaker Name:

Ankan Kheto ( Rollno : 521fp1002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

CH-113, Department of Food Process Engineering

Date and Time:

23 Jul 2026 5:00 PM

Contact:

Rachna Sehrawat

Abstract:

Currently, feeding the ever-increasing population (~1.07% per year) with nutrient-rich foods is a global concern. Guar seeds (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba L.) belong to the leguminous family and are a drought-resistant, sustainable crop, particularly rich in protein content (~27 to 32%). Considering these aspects, the alkaline isoelectric precipitation method was selected to isolate high-quality guar germ proteins (GGP) at different extraction pH levels (7 to 11). At pH 9, the protein efficiency ratio, essential amino acid index (46.53), predicted biological value (39.02), nutritional index (42.67), and protein purity (91.69%) were found to be higher than those at other pH conditions. With increasing extraction pH, in vitro protein digestibility (IVPD) of GGP samples improved from 83.92 to 92.2%. From SDS-PAGE, it was revealed that the band intensity (&lt10 kDa) became thinner with an increase in extraction pH from 7 to 9 and then thicker. Meanwhile, &beta-sheet content was the dominant secondary structure in GGP samples. Principal component analysis suggested that pH 9 was more suitable for isolating GGP, due to a superior nutritional profile and protein content. Furthermore, two novel technologies (cold plasma and superheated steam) were further utilized to improve the techno-functional properties of isolated GGP.&nbsp&nbsp

Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) was applied to guar germ protein isolates (GGPI, extracted at pH 9) at varying applied voltages (10, 20, and 30 kV) and durations (5 and 10 min). Multivariate analysis suggested that GGPI can be treated at 20 kV (5 and 10 min) to retain its nutritional properties while enhancing its functional attributes.&nbspThe effect of superheated steam (SHS) on the nutritional, structural, functional, and rheological properties of GGPI was examined at different temperatures (120, 130, and 140 &degC) and durations (5 and 10 min). SHS treatment significantly increased IVPD up to 130 ℃-10 min (89.08%). Multivariate analysis confirmed that SHS treatment could be more effective for preprocessing GGPI at 130 ℃ (5 and 10 min) to enhance solubility, digestibility, and gelling ability.

Furthermore, native and ACP (at 20 kV for 5 or 10 min) and SHS (at 130 &degC for 5 or 10 min) treated GGPI with were used to produce a concentrated emulsion (with coconut oil), which was then incorporated into frozen dessert. Most importantly, the structural recovery rate of all GGPI emulsions exceeded 89%, indicating superior thixotropic behaviour. In contrast, during frozen dessert melting, the friction factor was lowest for ACP-5 min emulsion-based frozen dessert. After adding saliva, ACP-5 min treated emulsion-based frozen dessert had comparable friction factor values at varying sliding speeds as milk cream-based frozen dessert. In summary, modified GGPI can partially replace milk proteins or other commercial plant proteins to develop hybrid or analogues of milk, beverages, frozen dessert, yogurt, and cheese.

Keywords: Plant proteins Structural modification Amino acids Rheology Emulsion Tribology.
